A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PIDDM and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated sections and retained experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original PDE benchmark comparisons, downstream-task experiments, ablations and synthetic MoG demonstrations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds compute comparisons, distributional measurements and component, robustness and optimization experiments.

M1.justification: The core teacher training, physics-informed distillation and masked latent inference remain unchanged. V2 adds a consistency-model distillation variant and an optional dynamic PDE-loss weighting procedure using detached running residual magnitudes (Table 4 and Appendix G.1). These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine PDE benchmarks and two MoG settings, retaining generation, Darcy forward/inverse solving and partial reconstruction. The new diagnostics reuse existing coverage; the added discussion of image inverse problems does not introduce evaluated image tasks.

E2.justification: The principal comparators—ECI, DiffusionPDE, D-Flow, PIDM and the unconstrained teacher—are retained; Teacher renames Vanilla in Table 1. V2 adds pure distillation controls in Tables 6–7 and RF-2, DMD and consistency-model comparisons without final-sample PDE supervision in Table 13.

E3.justification: V2 introduces FPD and SWD/APDD metrics, a same-hardware compute comparison with explicit forward/backward budgets, and checkpoint, backbone and optimization-iteration protocols. Table 3 uses different budgets from the original benchmark comparison. Appendix B also changes the stated MoG variance from 0.1 to 0.04 (standard deviation 0.2), aligning it with the main text without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Tables 6–13 investigate component attribution, diversity preservation, teacher-checkpoint sensitivity, U-Net/autoencoder robustness, dynamic weighting, latent convergence and initialization stability. They also isolate PDE supervision across distillation backbones. These substantially extend the existing sampling-step, loss-weight, hard-constraint and diffusion-schedule ablations.

E5.justification: V2 Table 12 newly reports MSE variance across random initializations for PIDDM-ref and DiffusionPDE on three downstream tasks. V1 has no corresponding uncertainty analysis. V2 does not specify the initialization count or seeds, so this establishes new variance reporting rather than a documented increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds FPD entries in Table 1, consistency-model results, compute/quality results in Table 3 and extensive diagnostic results in Tables 6–13. Existing reconstruction coefficient-MSE entries change from 0.913 to 0.091 for RF-2 and 0.954 to 0.095 for DMD, in the same 10^-1 units (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4). Most original benchmark values are retained; new budget-dependent results are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3 introduces a low-rank Gaussian setting and Theorems B.1–B.2 with proofs addressing slow constrained-coordinate score learning and constraint-error reduction through distillation. V2 also revises the earlier score derivation and corrects reverse-SDE and posterior-mean expressions. This is substantial formal content beyond the original derivations.

C1.justification: V2 replaces the central 'theoretically sound' contribution and unqualified distributional-fidelity assurance with a narrower claim about removing posterior-mean mismatch from the student objective, explicitly treating distributional fidelity as empirical. It withdraws the 'first' empirical-demonstration claim and strengthens the emphasis on robustness and minimal tuning.

C2.justification: V2 adds a mechanism explanation contrasting difficult constrained-score learning with penalizing final outputs, and interprets new controls as separating speed gains from physics-consistency gains. It also recasts unchanged Figure 3 as evidence of broad robustness, removing v1's explicit large-weight tradeoff and discretization-bias explanation. Teacher-quality and residual-operator limitations remain, with some tuning still acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 documents dynamic residual normalization toward 10^-4, distinguishes forward evaluations from inference-time backward passes and reports wall-clock seconds per sample. It corrects D-Flow's stated 50,000 NFEs to 5,000 for the unchanged 100-step-by-50-iteration procedure. Core FNO specifications, training settings, hardware and data-source information remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against inverse-problem diffusion methods, including DDRM, DDNM, LGD, DPG and approaches that reduce posterior approximation error. It credits earlier DPS discussion of Jensen's Gap and explicitly distinguishes PIDDM from Tee et al.'s similarly named Physics-Informed Distillation. These are substantive positioning changes beyond moving Related Work to Appendix A.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from main Section 2 to Appendix A, reorganizing the narrative and appendix sequence. The abstract, contribution statements, method explanations and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. V2 also changes citation style and adds an author, acknowledgements and an impact statement.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evidence displays with new Table 3 and Tables 6–13, adds FPD rows to Table 1 and a consistency-model column to the former Table 3. Figure 4 is redrawn with standardized color scales, and several displays are relocated or reformatted. Figures 2, 3 and 5 retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: The compute comparison and supervision-removal controls, especially Tables 3 and 13, substantially strengthen evidence for efficiency and the specific contribution of physics supervision. Added distributional diagnostics address weaknesses of relying mainly on moments, while narrower theoretical and novelty claims improve credibility. The weakened loss-weight caveats and incomplete reporting of new protocols remain drawbacks, but the improved experimental attribution and claim calibration provide a substantial net gain.
